system: You are the lead AI reviewer on a deal team. Read the following PRIMARY due-diligence documents and write a concise summary for the partner: key findings, red flags, and a recommendation. Connect issues across documents where relevant.

exchanges.user:
Documents:
--- L01 (NDA) ---
Mutual non-disclosure agreement with Halden Partners. Two-year term. Standard carve-outs. No non-solicitation clause.

--- L02 (Lease) ---
Head office lease, Level 3, 41 Coolidge Street. Five-year term from 2024, market rent review in year three. Landlord consent needed for assignment; clause 19 says a change of control is not an assignment.

--- L03 (Management accounts - revenue) ---
FY revenue AUD 18.4m, up 9%. Gross margin 61%. Largest customer Arlen Health, 41% of revenue; next largest customer 7%.

--- L04 (HR) ---
Headcount 94. Standard employment contracts. Twelve-month retention letters signed by the CTO and the Head of Sales.

--- L05 (Customer contract) ---
Master services agreement with Arlen Health, renewed 1 July 2025 for five years. Services: platform licence, hosting and support. Fees: annual, CPI-indexed, invoiced quarterly in advance. Service levels: 99.9% monthly uptime; service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. Data: customer data hosted in Australia; ISO 27001 certification maintained. Liability: capped at twelve months' fees, except data breach (three times annual fees). Termination: either party for material breach not remedied within 30 days; the Customer may also terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice at any time within six months after a change in control of the Supplier, with no early-termination fee. Governing law: New South Wales. Notices: by email to nominated contacts.

--- L06 (Bank facility) ---
AUD 6m revolving facility with Southgate Bank, expiring 2027. Leverage covenant: net debt to EBITDA not more than 2.5x, tested quarterly.

--- L07 (Email) ---
Email from the CFO, M. Iredale, to the Chair, 14 April: 'To be clear for the board pack: we breached the leverage covenant at the 31 March test date, 2.9x against the 2.5x limit. The bank has not been notified yet. I will raise it with them after the board meeting.'

--- L08 (Internal note) ---
Note from the Head of Customer Success, T. Okafor: 'I can't be sure, but the uptick in small-business churn this quarter might be linked to the January price change. It's too early to say, and the numbers are small.'

--- L09 (Insurance) ---
Professional indemnity and cyber cover to AUD 10m, renewed in March. No notified claims.

--- L10 (IP) ---
Platform code written by employees under standard IP assignment clauses. Two open-source components, under MIT and Apache 2.0 licences.

--- L11 (Supplier) ---
Hosting with a major cloud provider on standard online terms. Monthly billing, no minimum commitment.

--- L12 (Board minutes) ---
Board meeting, 20 March. Approved the FY budget and hiring plan. Noted a strong sales pipeline. No other business.

--- L13 (Policy) ---
Privacy policy updated for the 2025 amendments. Annual staff privacy training completed.

--- L14 (Vendor contract) ---
Office cleaning contract, twelve months, terminable on 30 days' notice.

--- L15 (Fixed assets) ---
Laptops and office fit-out. Written-down value AUD 0.4m.

Write the DD summary now.
exchanges.text:
## Partner DD summary

**Recommendation: do not proceed unconditionally.** The key risks are a change-of-control exit right for the dominant customer and a documented bank covenant breach. Resolve both before commitment and reflect any residual exposure in valuation and deal protections.

### Key findings and red flags

- **41% of revenue exposed to post-acquisition termination.** Arlen Health represents approximately **AUD 7.5m of annual revenue**. Despite its five-year renewal, Arlen may terminate for convenience on 90 days’ notice during the six months after a supplier change of control, without an early-termination fee. The stated contract term therefore does not secure this revenue through a sale. Seek a binding waiver of this right or equivalent contractual commitment before closing. (L03, L05)

- **Leverage covenant breached; remediation unverified.** The CFO’s 14 April email confirms leverage of **2.9x against a 2.5x limit** at 31 March and says the bank had not yet been notified. The documents do not establish subsequent notification, waiver or cure. Review default, notification and enforcement provisions; obtain current covenant calculations and written bank resolution. Arlen revenue loss could further pressure EBITDA and covenant compliance. The delayed notification also warrants scrutiny of financial controls and board escalation. (L06–L07)

- **Arlen’s data obligations create material contingent exposure.** Its contract requires Australian hosting and maintained ISO 27001 certification, with data-breach liability capped at three times annual fees—potentially around **AUD 22.6m**, using its reported revenue contribution as a proxy. That exceeds the stated **AUD 10m** insurance cover; actual fee basis, policy coverage and exclusions require verification. Confirm hosting location, certification and incident history; “no notified claims” does not establish no incidents. (L03, L05, L09, L11)

### Other findings

- Revenue grew **9% to AUD 18.4m**, with a **61% gross margin**, but customer concentration is substantial. The suggested link between small-business churn and January pricing is explicitly tentative; validate cohort data before attributing causation. (L03, L08)
- CTO and Head of Sales have signed 12-month retention letters; confirm commencement dates, enforceability and post-close coverage. Employee IP assignments and permissive open-source licences are positive, subject to ownership and licence-compliance verification. (L04, L10)
- For a share acquisition, the office lease expressly excludes change of control from assignment; an asset transfer may still require consent. Factor in the year-three market rent review. Privacy policies and training are positive indicators, not proof of operational compliance. (L02, L13)

**Deal approach:** make Arlen protection and bank waiver/refinancing conditions to closing; stress-test customer-loss liquidity and debt capacity. Use targeted warranties and appropriate price adjustment, escrow or indemnities for unresolved exposures—not as substitutes for preserving the customer relationship and financing.
